claim: Iridescent plumage colors are produced by nanostructures in feathers.
source: The brilliant iridescent plumage of birds creates some of the most stunning color displays known in the natural world. Iridescent plumage colors are produced by nanostructures in feathers and have evolved in diverse birds.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a factual assertion about the mechanism of iridescent color production.

claim: Iridescent plumage has evolved in diverse birds.
source: Iridescent plumage colors are produced by nanostructures in feathers and have evolved in diverse birds.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the abstract.

claim: The building blocks of iridescent nanostructures are melanosomes (melanin-filled organelles).
source: The building blocks of these structures—melanosomes (melanin-filled organelles)—come in a variety of forms, yet how these different forms contribute to color production across birds remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a factual description of the structural components.

claim: Melanosomes come in a variety of forms.
source: The building blocks of these structures—melanosomes (melanin-filled organelles)—come in a variety of forms, yet how these different forms contribute to color production across birds remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the abstract.

claim: A key feature that unites all melanosome forms in brilliant iridescent structures is thin melanin layers.
source: We find that a key feature that unites all melanosome forms in brilliant iridescent structures is thin melanin layers.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by the study's analyses.

claim: Birds have achieved thin melanin layers by decreasing the size of the melanosome directly.
source: Birds have achieved this in multiple ways: by decreasing the size of the melanosome directly, by hollowing out the interior, or by flattening the melanosome into a platelet.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract, describing mechanisms observed in the study.

claim: Birds have achieved thin melanin layers by hollowing out the interior of melanosomes.
source: Birds have achieved this in multiple ways: by decreasing the size of the melanosome directly, by hollowing out the interior, or by flattening the melanosome into a platelet.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: Birds have achieved thin melanin layers by flattening the melanosome into a platelet.
source: Birds have achieved this in multiple ways: by decreasing the size of the melanosome directly, by hollowing out the interior, or by flattening the melanosome into a platelet.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: The evolution of thin melanin layers more than doubles the range of colors that can be produced with a thick melanin layer.
source: The evolution of thin melanin layers unlocks color-producing possibilities, more than doubling the range of colors that can be produced with a thick melanin layer and simultaneously increasing brightness.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract, quantifying the effect of thin melanin layers on color diversity.

claim: The evolution of thin melanin layers simultaneously increases brightness.
source: The evolution of thin melanin layers unlocks color-producing possibilities, more than doubling the range of colors that can be produced with a thick melanin layer and simultaneously increasing brightness.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: Structural colors greatly expand the range of colors birds can produce with their feathers relative to pigment-based mechanisms.
source: In birds, structural colors greatly expand—relative to pigment-based mechanisms—the range of colors birds can produce with their feathers (Stoddard and Prum, 2011; Maia et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is stated as a fact supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Some structural colors are iridescent, where the perceived hue changes with viewing or lighting angle.
source: Some structural colors are iridescent: the perceived hue changes with viewing or lighting angle.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about iridescent colors.

claim: Iridescent coloration features prominently in the dynamic courtship displays of many bird species, including birds-of-paradise (Paradisaeidae), hummingbirds (Trochilidae), and pheasants (Phasianidae).
source: Iridescent coloration features prominently in the dynamic courtship displays of many bird species, including birds-of-paradise (Paradisaeidae), hummingbirds (Trochilidae), and pheasants (Phasianidae) (Greenewalt et al., 1960; Stavenga et al., 2015; Zi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a fact supported by citations.

claim: All iridescent feather coloration is produced by nanostructures in the feather barbules consisting of melanosomes and keratin.
source: All iridescent feather coloration is produced by nanostructures in the feather barbules consisting of melanin-filled organelles (melanosomes) and keratin (Figure 1), but brilliant iridescent coloration arises from light interference by photonic crystal-like structures (henceforth photonic crystals), while weak iridescent coloration is produced by structures with a single layer of melanosomes (Durrer, 1977).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with reference to Figure 1 and citation to Durrer, 1977.

claim: Brilliant iridescent coloration arises from light interference by photonic crystal-like structures.
source: All iridescent feather coloration is produced by nanostructures in the feather barbules consisting of melanin-filled organelles (melanosomes) and keratin (Figure 1), but brilliant iridescent coloration arises from light interference by photonic crystal-like structures (henceforth photonic crystals), while weak iridescent coloration is produced by structures with a single layer of melanosomes (Durrer, 1977).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to Durrer, 1977.

claim: Weak iridescent coloration is produced by structures with a single layer of melanosomes.
source: All iridescent feather coloration is produced by nanostructures in the feather barbules consisting of melanin-filled organelles (melanosomes) and keratin (Figure 1), but brilliant iridescent coloration arises from light interference by photonic crystal-like structures (henceforth photonic crystals), while weak iridescent coloration is produced by structures with a single layer of melanosomes (Durrer, 1977).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to Durrer, 1977.

claim: A photonic crystal is defined by having periodic changes in refractive index.
source: A photonic crystal is defined by having periodic changes in refractive index (Joannopoulos et al., 2008); in feather barbules, this is created by periodic arrangements of melanosomes in keratin.
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by citation.

claim: In feather barbules, periodic changes in refractive index are created by periodic arrangements of melanosomes in keratin.
source: A photonic crystal is defined by having periodic changes in refractive index (Joannopoulos et al., 2008); in feather barbules, this is created by periodic arrangements of melanosomes in keratin.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about feather structure.

claim: A photonic crystal greatly amplifies color saturation and brightness compared to a single-layered structure by adding more reflection interfaces.
source: By adding more reflection interfaces, a photonic crystal greatly amplifies color saturation and brightness compared to a single-layered structure, the latter of which typically functions as a simple thin film (Kinoshita et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to support the optical principle.

claim: Durrer, 1977 classified melanosomes into five main types: thick solid rods (S-type), thin solid rods (St-type), hollow rods (R-type), platelets (P-type), and hollow platelets (K-type).
source: Durrer, 1977 classified melanosomes into five main types: (1) thick solid rods (S-type, Figure 2A); (2) thin solid rods (St-type, Figure 2B); (3) hollow rods (with an air-filled interior, R-type, Figure 2C); (4) platelets (P-type, Figure 2D); and (5) hollow platelets (K-type, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to Durrer, 1977 and reference to Figure 2.

claim: All five melanosome types occur in single-layered structures producing weak iridescence.
source: All five melanosome types occur in single-layered structures producing weak iridescence.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the introduction.

claim: Four melanosome types (all but thick solid rods) occur in photonic crystals producing brilliant iridescence.
source: Four of these types—all but thick solid rods—occur in photonic crystals producing brilliant iridescence.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the introduction.

claim: The shape of melanosomes in other melanized vertebrate tissues, including black and gray feathers, is typically a solid rod.
source: This diversity is extraordinary given that the shape of melanosomes in other melanized vertebrate tissues, including black and gray feathers, is typically a solid rod (D'Alba and Shawkey, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation.

claim: The thick solid rods found in weakly iridescent feathers resemble the melanosomes found in plain black feathers.
source: The thick solid rods found in weakly iridescent feathers resemble the melanosomes found in plain black feathers (Durrer, 1977) and are likely ancestral to the four more modified, derived melanosome shapes (Shawkey et al., 2006; Maia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citations.

claim: Thick solid rods are likely ancestral to the four more modified, derived melanosome shapes.
source: The thick solid rods found in weakly iridescent feathers resemble the melanosomes found in plain black feathers (Durrer, 1977) and are likely ancestral to the four more modified, derived melanosome shapes (Shawkey et al., 2006; Maia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as an inference supported by citations.

claim: The evolution of hollow and/or platelet-shaped melanosomes in African starlings (Sturnidae) was associated with great expansions in color diversity and increases in brilliance.
source: Supporting this idea, Maia et al., 2013b showed that the evolution of hollow and/or platelet-shaped melanosomes in African starlings (Sturnidae) was associated with great expansions in color diversity and increases in brilliance.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a cited study.

claim: Hollow rods increase the brightness of iridescent colors compared to structures with solid rods.
source: Moreover, Eliason et al., 2013 used optical modeling and plumage color measurements of the violet-backed starling (Cinnyricinclus leucogaster) and wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) to show that hollow rods increase the brightness of iridescent colors compared to structures with solid rods.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a cited study.

claim: Iridescent feather nanostructures have been described in 306 bird species representing 15 different orders and 35 families.
source: We found that iridescent feather nanostructures have been described in 306 bird species representing 15 different orders and 35 families.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the feather iridescence database compilation.

claim: Solid rods can be divided into two distinct distributions (a thinner and thicker variety).
source: Analyzing the distribution of melanosome diameter in all solid rods, we found a significant bimodal distribution (Figure 4, unimodality rejected, p<0.001, bimodality not rejected, p=0.888).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 4.

claim: Thick solid rods are defined as those with a diameter ≥190 nm.
source: Based on the bimodal distribution of melanosome diameters in solid rods, we define 'thick solid rods' as those with a diameter ≥190 nm and 'thin solid rods' as those with a diameter <190 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a definition based on the data analysis.

claim: Thin solid rods are defined as those with a diameter <190 nm.
source: Based on the bimodal distribution of melanosome diameters in solid rods, we define 'thick solid rods' as those with a diameter ≥190 nm and 'thin solid rods' as those with a diameter <190 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a definition based on the data analysis.

claim: Thick solid rods are similar in size to melanosomes in black feathers.
source: Thick solid rods are similar in size to melanosomes in black feathers (Figure 4; data from Li et al., 2012), supporting the hypothesis that thick solid rods represent minimally modified or unmodified melanosomes.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 4 and data from Li et al., 2012.

claim: All hollow and/or platelet-shaped melanosomes can be classified as having thin melanin layers (range 24–139 nm).
source: Using this new definition, we found that all hollow and/or platelet-shaped melanosomes can indeed be classified as having thin melanin layers (range 24–139 nm, Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 5.

claim: All four derived melanosomes with thin melanin layers have significantly thinner melanin layers than melanosomes in black feathers and thick solid rods.
source: All four derived melanosomes with thin melanin layers have significantly thinner melanin layers than melanosomes in black feathers and thick solid rods (phylogenetic pairwise t-test, all p<0.01, see details in Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with statistical support.

claim: All derived melanosome types have converged on thicknesses well within the expected range of 37.5–206 nm.
source: We found that all derived melanosomes indeed have converged on thicknesses well within this expected range (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 5.

claim: 99% of all species with photonic crystals contain melanosomes with thin melanin layers.
source: We also found that the vast majority of photonic crystals contain melanosomes with thin melanin layers (99% of all species with photonic crystals).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the database analysis.

claim: Over 80% of all families represented in the feather iridescence database have evolved thin melanin layers (27 out of 32 families).
source: Over 80% of all families represented in the feather iridescence database have evolved thin melanin layers (27 out of 32 families, Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Air pocket diameter ranged from 50 to 251 nm and did not differ significantly between rods and platelets.
source: Air pocket diameter ranged from 50 to 251 nm and did not differ significantly between rods and platelets (phylogenetic ANOVA, F(1, 55)=16.80, p=0.176, df=1).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with statistical support.

claim: A hollow interior has evolved in at least 12 bird families, or 34% of all families in the feather iridescence database.
source: Our phylogenetic analysis shows that a hollow interior has evolved in at least 12 bird families, or 34% of all families in the feather iridescence database (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from phylogenetic analysis with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Platelets are present in 11 bird families, or 31% of all families represented in the feather iridescence database.
source: Platelets are present in 11 bird families, or 31% of all families represented in the feather iridescence database (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: There was no significant difference between number of layers in structures with platelets compared to rods.
source: We did not find support for the hypothesis that platelets allow birds to incorporate a greater number of layers in the iridescent structure. There was no significant difference between number of layers in structures with platelets compared to rods (phylogenetic ANOVA, F(1, 220)=21.88, p=0.321).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with statistical support.

claim: Optical modeling revealed that thick solid rods are severely constrained in color diversity.
source: Optical modeling revealed that thick solid rods are severely constrained in color diversity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from optical modeling with reference to Figure 6A.

claim: All four derived melanosome types with thin melanin layers are capable of producing a large range of saturated colors.
source: In contrast, all four derived melanosome types with thin melanin layers are capable of producing a large range of saturated colors (Figure 6B–E).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from optical modeling with reference to Figure 6B-E.

claim: Color diversity (color span and voxel occupancy) is very similar for the four derived types.
source: Color diversity (color span and voxel occupancy) is very similar for the four derived types, suggesting that melanin thinness—the only modification they all share—is the most important modification for achieving saturated and varied colors (Figure 6K–L).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from optical modeling with reference to Figure 6K-L.

claim: Melanin layer thickness explained the greatest amount of variation in saturation in the linear model.
source: In agreement with the results for color space occupancy (Figure 6A–E), melanin layer thickness explained the greatest amount of variation in saturation in our linear model (Figure 6M; gray points).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the linear model analysis with reference to Figure 6M.

claim: All modifications increase brightness, but this effect is strongest for the interaction of hollowness and platelet shape.
source: The linear model yielded similar results for both of our brightness measures (Figure 6N–O; gray points). All modifications increase brightness, but this effect is strongest for the interaction of hollowness and platelet shape (Figure 6N–O; gray points).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the linear model analysis with reference to Figure 6N-O.

claim: The optical model predicts that hollow platelets produce the brightest colors.
source: Thus, the optical model predicts that hollow platelets produce the brightest colors.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the optical model.

claim: Spectral data were collected from 111 patches on 80 species that were represented in the feather iridescence database and possessed known melanosome types.
source: We collected spectral data from 111 patches on 80 species that were represented in the feather iridescence database and possessed known melanosome types.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the data collection.

claim: The color diversity of structures with thick solid rods is low, almost half of that found in structures with thin melanin layers.
source: In agreement with the optical model results, the color diversity of structures with thick solid rods is low, almost half of that found in structures with thin melanin layers (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the plumage data analysis with reference to Figure 6F.

claim: Thin solid rods, hollow rods, solid platelets, and hollow platelets are all nearly equal in color diversity.
source: Moreover—mirroring the results in our optical model simulations—thin solid rods, hollow rods, solid platelets, and hollow platelets are all nearly equal in color diversity (Figure 6K–L).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the plumage data analysis with reference to Figure 6K-L.

claim: The linear model revealed a significant positive effect of hollowness and platelet shape on the brightness of colors.
source: In agreement with the optical model, the linear model revealed a significant positive effect of hollowness and platelet shape on the brightness of colors (Figure 6N–O; black points).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the linear model analysis with reference to Figure 6N-O.

claim: Photonic crystals produce colors of significantly higher saturation than single-layered structures.
source: The model also confirms that photonic crystals produce colors of significantly higher saturation than single-layered structures (Figure 6M; black points).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the linear model analysis with reference to Figure 6M.

claim: Saturation increases for structures with melanin layer thickness <190 nm.
source: Specifically, we find that saturation increases for structures with melanin layer thickness <190 nm (Figure 6A–E, Figure 6—figure supplement 2), which we define as 'thin melanin layers.'
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to figures.

claim: Above 190 nm melanin layer thickness, iridescent structures produce colors that have low saturation and brightness, irrespective of the number of melanosome layers.
source: Above this value, iridescent structures produce colors that have low saturation and brightness, irrespective of the number of melanosome layers (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 6A.

claim: The preserved melanosomes from the plumage of Microraptor have an average diameter of 196 nm.
source: For example, the preserved melanosomes from the plumage of Microraptor, a feathered theropod that is predicted to have exhibited iridescent plumage, have an average diameter of 196 nm (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to Li et al., 2012.

claim: Microraptor exhibited weak iridescence, as opposed to brilliant iridescence.
source: This suggests that Microraptor exhibited weak iridescence, as opposed to brilliant iridescence.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the melanosome diameter data.

claim: Photonic crystals with all four melanosome types found in brilliant iridescent structures have similar optical qualities.
source: Our results show that photonic crystals with all four melanosome types found in brilliant iridescent structures have similar optical qualities.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's results.

claim: Variability in melanosome type may be strongly influenced by historical factors, as opposed to particular types being associated with specific optical functions.
source: This suggests that variability in melanosome type may be strongly influenced by historical factors, as opposed to particular types being associated with specific optical functions.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: In Galliformes, some families have photonic crystals with thin solid rods and others have photonic crystals with hollow rods.
source: In Galliformes, some families have photonic crystals with thin solid rods and others have photonic crystals with hollow rods (Figure 3A), but these different structures have almost certainly evolved from an ancestor with a non-iridescent or single-layered structure rather than a photonic crystal (Gammie, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with reference to Figure 3A and citation to Gammie, 2013.

claim: In Sturnidae, photonic crystals with hollow rods in the genus Cinnyricinclus and photonic crystals with hollow platelets in the genus Lamprotornis likely evolved independently from non-iridescent structures.
source: Similarly, in Sturnidae, photonic crystals with hollow rods in the genus Cinnyricinclus and photonic crystals with hollow platelets in the genus Lamprotornis likely evolved independently from non-iridescent structures (Figure 3A, Durrer and Villiger, 1970; Maia et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is stated as an inference with reference to Figure 3A and citations.

claim: In the birds-of-paradise (Paradisaeidae), two species (Paradisaea rubra and Parotia lawesii) are known to have evolved large rods with a porous interior.
source: In the birds-of-paradise (Paradisaeidae), which typically display photonic crystals with thin solid rods, two species (Paradisaea rubra and Parotia lawesii) are known to have evolved large rods with a porous interior (Figure 5, Durrer, 1977; Stavenga et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with reference to Figure 5 and citations.

claim: In Lawes' parotia (Parotia lawesii), other iridescent patches contain structures with thin solid rods, proving interpatch variability in melanosome type.
source: In Lawes' parotia (Parotia lawesii), other iridescent patches contain structures with thin solid rods, proving interpatch variability in melanosome type.
evidence: This is stated as a fact demonstrating variability.

claim: Hummingbirds can exhibit interpatch variability in melanosome type, with some patches containing structures with solid platelets, or even mixed structures with both hollow and solid platelets.
source: Hummingbirds, whose iridescent structures are typically built with hollow platelets, can also exhibit interpatch variability in melanosome type. Some patches may contain a structure with solid platelets, or even mixed structures with both hollow and solid platelets (Gruson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to Gruson et al., 2019.

claim: The only known examples of interpatch variability in melanosome type come from the birds-of-paradise and hummingbirds.
source: It is notable that the only known examples of interpatch variability in melanosome type come from the birds-of-paradise and hummingbirds—groups that are known to have exceptionally high rates of color evolution (Beltrán et al., 2021; Eliason et al., 2020; Ligon et al., 2018; Parra, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citations supporting the high rates of color evolution.

claim: Birds-of-paradise and hummingbirds are groups that are known to have exceptionally high rates of color evolution.
source: It is notable that the only known examples of interpatch variability in melanosome type come from the birds-of-paradise and hummingbirds—groups that are known to have exceptionally high rates of color evolution (Beltrán et al., 2021; Eliason et al., 2020; Ligon et al., 2018; Parra, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citations.

claim: Both birds-of-paradise and hummingbirds typically have >9 melanosome layers in their iridescent structures.
source: Both birds-of-paradise and hummingbirds typically have >9 melanosome layers in their iridescent structures, which already achieves nearly 100% reflectance irrespective of melanosome type.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the structure of these groups.

claim: Gruson et al., 2019 found color production to be similar among patches with different melanosome types in hummingbirds.
source: Indeed, Gruson et al., 2019 found color production to be similar among patches with different melanosome types in hummingbirds.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a cited study.

claim: Melanin has been shown to influence a feather's mechanical properties.
source: Melanin has been shown to influence a feather's mechanical properties (Burtt, 1979) and ability to resist bacterial degradation (Goldstein et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation.

claim: Melanin has been shown to influence a feather's ability to resist bacterial degradation.
source: Melanin has been shown to influence a feather's mechanical properties (Burtt, 1979) and ability to resist bacterial degradation (Goldstein et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation.

claim: Structures with derived melanosomes have converged on a shared range of melanin layer thicknesses.
source: Our results show that structures with derived melanosomes have converged on a shared range of melanin layer thicknesses (Figure 5), which suggests that differences in melanin content may not be large.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Brilliant iridescent structures likely originated from single-layered structures with thick solid rods.
source: Brilliant iridescent structures likely originated from single-layered structures with thick solid rods (Maia et al., 2012; Shawkey et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as an inference supported by citations.

claim: Single-layered structures with modified melanosomes are relatively common.
source: Single-layered structures with modified melanosomes are relatively common (Figure 5), suggesting that Path 1—where melanosome shape diversifies first—may be a common route to more complex structures.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Hexagonally arranged photonic crystals with hollow rods are common in many groups (Galliformes and Trogoniformes) that also contain taxa with single-layered structures of thick solid rods.
source: In support of Path 2, hexagonally arranged photonic crystals with hollow rods are common in many groups (Galliformes and Trogoniformes) that also contain taxa with single-layered structures of thick solid rods.
evidence: This is stated as a fact supporting an evolutionary hypothesis.

claim: A vaned feather consists of branching structures where the barbules are the interlocking filaments.
source: A vaned feather (A) consists of branching structures where the barbules (B) are the interlocking filaments.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 1 as a description of feather anatomy.

claim: A cross-section of a barbule from an iridescent feather reveals the intricate nanostructure responsible for the color, consisting of layers of melanosomes in keratin.
source: A cross-section of a barbule from an iridescent feather (C) reveals the intricate nanostructure responsible for the color, consisting of layers of melanosomes in keratin (D).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 1 with reference to the figure panels.

claim: A single-layered structure with thick solid rods gives rise to the dark, black-blue iridescence of a brown-headed cowbird (Molothrus ater).
source: A single-layered structure with thick solid rods (A) gives rise to the dark, black-blue iridescence of a brown-headed cowbird (Molothrus ater).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: Single-layered structures generally give rise to 'weak' iridescent colors, with low color saturation and brightness.
source: This type of structure generally gives rise to 'weak' iridescent colors, with low color saturation and brightness.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 as a general principle.

claim: Photonic crystals with multiple layers of melanosomes generally give rise to 'brilliant' iridescent colors, with high saturation and brightness.
source: Photonic crystals (B–E) with multiple layers of melanosomes generally give rise to 'brilliant' iridescent colors, with high saturation and brightness.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 as a general principle.

claim: Thin solid rods in a multilayer configuration produce the iridescent colors of the Nicobar pigeon (Caloenas nicobarica).
source: Thin solid rods (B) in a multilayer configuration (also called a one-dimensional photonic crystal) produce the iridescent colors of the Nicobar pigeon (Caloenas nicobarica).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: In the elegant trogon (Trogon elegans), the iridescent green color is produced by hexagonally packed hollow rods.
source: In the elegant trogon (Trogon elegans), the iridescent green color is produced by hexagonally packed hollow rods (C).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: Sunbird barbules contain melanosomes stacked in multilayers, with solid platelet-shaped melanosomes serving as the building blocks.
source: Sunbird (here the variable sunbird, Cinnyris venustus) barbules contain melanosomes stacked in multilayers, with solid platelet-shaped melanosomes serving as the building blocks (D).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: Hollow platelets form multilayer configurations in many hummingbird species.
source: The fifth melanosome type is a hollow platelet (E), which forms multilayer configurations in many hummingbird species (here a ruby-throated hummingbird, Archilochus colubris).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: The five types of melanosomes are characterized by different combinations of three key modifications: thin melanin layers, hollowness, and platelet shape.
source: The five types of melanosomes are characterized by different combinations of three key modifications: thin melanin layers, hollowness, and platelet shape, which are indicated as symbols under each melanosome type.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2.

claim: Thin melanin layers are present in four melanosome types.
source: Thin melanin layers are present in four melanosome types, but they are achieved in different ways, as is shown by the schematic in (F).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: Solid forms translate to a single melanin layer, while hollow forms create two thinner melanin layers intersected by an air layer.
source: A simplified diagram of each melanosome type (F, right) shows how solid forms translate to a single melanin layer, while hollow forms create two thinner melanin layers intersected by an air layer.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 2 with reference to the figure panel.

claim: The majority of bird families with iridescent plumage studied have evolved thin melanin layers.
source: The majority of bird families with iridescent plumage studied have evolved thin melanin layers, and there are no hollow or platelet-shaped melanosomes that have not also evolved this modification.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 3B.

claim: There are no hollow or platelet-shaped melanosomes that have not also evolved thin melanin layers.
source: The majority of bird families with iridescent plumage studied have evolved thin melanin layers, and there are no hollow or platelet-shaped melanosomes that have not also evolved this modification.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 3B.

claim: A similar number of families have hollow or platelet-shaped melanosomes, but only five families have evolved both modifications together.
source: A similar number of families have hollow or platelet-shaped melanosomes, but only five families have evolved both modifications together.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 3B.

claim: Solid rods can be divided into a thinner variety (diameter of ~100 nm) and thicker variety (diameter of ~200 nm).
source: This is plausible based on the measurements and description of melanosome types given by Durrer, 1977, who proposed a division of solid rods into a thinner (diameter of ~100 nm) and thicker variety (diameter of ~200 nm), but has not been formally quantified.
evidence: This is stated as a fact from Durrer, 1977.

claim: The melanosomes in black feathers are considerably thicker than the thin solid rods in iridescent feathers.
source: In contrast, the melanosomes in black feathers are considerably thicker than the thin solid rods in iridescent feathers (Figure 4), suggesting that thin solid rods are considerably modified from the ancestral state.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 4.

claim: All hollow forms in photonic crystals have a single melanin wall thickness of <95 nm.
source: However, all hollow forms in photonic crystals have a single melanin wall thickness of <95 nm (Figure 5), so they would still qualify as 'thin' even if this value were doubled.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Many single-layered structures are formed with melanosomes with thin melanin layers (present in 59% of all species with single-layered structures).
source: However, it is also true that many single-layered structures are formed with melanosomes with thin melanin layers (present in 59% of all species with single-layered structures).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the database analysis.

claim: Three species are recorded to have thick solid rods in a photonic crystal: Paradisaea rubra (Red bird-of-paradise), Parotia lawesii (Lawes' parotia), and Eudynamys scolopaceus (Asian koel).
source: Note that three species are recorded to have thick solid rods in a photonic crystal: Paradisaea rubra (Red bird-of-paradise), Parotia lawesii (Lawes' parotia), and Eudynamys scolopaceus (Asian koel).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 5.

claim: Paradisaea rubra and Parotia lawesii have melanosomes with porous interiors.
source: Paradisaea rubra and Parotia lawesii have melanosomes with porous interiors (see Discussion), so they are not 'true' thick solid rods and will have an optical thickness closer to that of a derived melanosome.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 5.

claim: The structure in Eudynamys scolopaceus consists of tightly, hexagonally packed rods and appears to produce relatively weak iridescent color.
source: The structure in Eudynamys scolopaceus consists of tightly, hexagonally packed rods and appears to produce relatively weak iridescent color.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 5.

claim: Thick solid rods produce colors of substantially lower diversity and saturation than all melanosome types with thin melanin layers.
source: Thick solid rods produce colors of substantially lower diversity and saturation (A, F) than all melanosome types with thin melanin layers (B–E, G–J).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6 with reference to the figure panels.

claim: Hollowness and platelet shape do not affect color diversity notably.
source: In contrast, hollowness and platelet shape do not affect color diversity notably (C–E, H–J).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6 with reference to the figure panels.

claim: Saturation is low for all single-layered structures, with the exception of hollow platelets.
source: Note that saturation is low for all single-layered structures, with the exception of hollow platelets (E).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Data for hollow platelets in single-layered structures are mainly collected from African starlings.
source: Data for (E) are mainly collected from African starlings; thus, it is not clear whether this is a general trend or specific to this group.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Single-layered structures behave differently from photonic crystals and deserve further study.
source: Either way, it demonstrates that single-layered structures behave differently from photonic crystals and deserve further study.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The distribution of melanosome size in solid rods suggests that there is a shift at approximately 190 nm.
source: Histogram in the background shows the size distribution of solid rods in iridescent feather structures (data from feather iridescence database). Both the results of the optical model and the distribution of melanosome size in solid rods suggest that there is a shift at approximately 190 nm, which we have defined as the dividing line between thin and thick melanin layers.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: For the production of weakly iridescent colors, it is sufficient to organize a single layer of melanosomes of any size, since it is typically the thickness of the overlying keratin cortex that controls the interference color.
source: For the production of weakly iridescent colors, it is sufficient to organize a single layer of melanosomes of any size, since it is typically the thickness of the overlying keratin cortex that controls the interference color (Doucet et al., 2006; Maia et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citations.

claim: Durrer, 1977 observed that a photonic crystal and melanin layers with an optical thickness <λ/2 were common to the brilliant structures he studied.
source: Indeed, Durrer, 1977 observed that these two features were common to the brilliant structures he studied and here we validate the importance of his observation with optical modeling and plumage color measurements.
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation to Durrer, 1977.

claim: Diverse photonic crystals in birds often have independent evolutionary origins.
source: Supporting this interpretation is the fact that diverse photonic crystals in birds often have independent evolutionary origins.
evidence: This is stated as a fact supporting an interpretation.

claim: Iridescent structures most likely evolved from black plumage.
source: Iridescent structures most likely evolved from black plumage (Maia et al., 2012; Shawkey et al., 2006); therefore, we can use the size of melanosomes in black feathers to represent an 'unmodified' melanosome.
evidence: This is stated as an inference supported by citations.

claim: The typical diameter of melanosomes found in vertebrates is ~300 nm.
source: The typical diameter of melanosomes found in vertebrates is ~300 nm (Li et al., 2014), exceeding this range.
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation.

claim: For iridescent structures producing first-order interference peaks, melanin layer thickness is expected to be below 206 nm.
source: Thus, for iridescent structures producing first-order interference peaks, we expect melanin layer thickness to be below 206 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical prediction based on optical principles.

claim: A lower limit for melanin layer thickness is expected at 37.5 nm, since melanin layer thickness is unlikely to have evolved below the thickness required for maximum reflectance at ultraviolet wavelengths.
source: Moreover, we expect a lower limit at 37.5 nm, since melanin layer thickness is unlikely to have evolved below the thickness required for maximum reflectance at ultraviolet wavelengths.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical prediction.

claim: The expected range for melanin layer thickness in iridescent structures is 37.5–206 nm.
source: This gives us an expected range of 37.5–206 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical prediction based on optical principles.

claim: A hollow interior could increase reflectance by creating a sharper contrast in refractive index in the structure.
source: A hollow interior could increase reflectance by creating a sharper contrast in refractive index in the structure (Durrer, 1977; Eliason et al., 2013; Kinoshita, 2008; Land, 1972; Stavenga et al., 2018), making a color brighter.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: The refractive index of air (n=1) is lower than that of keratin (n=1.56).
source: This is because the refractive index of air (n=1) is lower than that of keratin (n=1.56).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about refractive indices.

claim: The expected range for air layer thickness is 75–350 nm.
source: Thus, the expected range is 75–350 nm.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical prediction based on optical principles.

claim: Platelet-shaped melanosomes have been hypothesized to increase reflection by creating smooth, mirror-like reflection surfaces.
source: Platelet-shaped melanosomes have been hypothesized to increase reflection by creating smooth, mirror-like reflection surfaces (Durrer, 1977; Land, 1972).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis with citations.

claim: The thin platelet shape might allow for more layers to be packed within a photonic crystal, which would increase total reflection.
source: Moreover, the thin platelet shape might allow for more layers to be packed within a photonic crystal, which would increase total reflection (Maia et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis with citation.

claim: In single-layered structures, the layer of melanosomes only functions to delimit the keratin layer, so the thickness of the melanin layer itself is largely irrelevant.
source: The layer of melanosomes only functions to delimit the keratin layer, so the thickness of the melanin layer itself is largely irrelevant.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for why thick solid rods persist in single-layered structures.

claim: There would be no selection pressure to decrease melanin layer thickness in single-layered structures.
source: Thus, there would be no selection pressure to decrease melanin layer thickness in single-layered structures, and we would expect the ancestral condition (thick solid rods) to remain.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about evolutionary selection.

claim: The diverse melanosome types found in brilliant iridescent structures evolved to generate thin melanin layers in different ways.
source: We suggest that the diverse melanosome types found in brilliant iridescent structures evolved to generate thin melanin layers in different ways.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The feather iridescence database covers 47 studies from 1952 to 2020.
source: In total, our database covers 47 studies from 1952 to 2020 and 306 unique species, across 35 families and 15 orders (37% of total orders and 14% of total families in Aves, after taxonomy in Billerman et al., 2020.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the database.

claim: The database represents 37% of total orders and 14% of total families in Aves.
source: In total, our database covers 47 studies from 1952 to 2020 and 306 unique species, across 35 families and 15 orders (37% of total orders and 14% of total families in Aves, after taxonomy in Billerman et al., 2020.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the database coverage.

claim: Descriptions for only 61% of species included details about melanin layer thickness.
source: For example, descriptions for only 61% of species included details about melanin layer thickness, while descriptions for almost all species had complete information on the presence/absence of melanosome hollowness and/or platelet shape (92%).
evidence: This is stated as a description of data completeness.

claim: Descriptions for almost all species (92%) had complete information on the presence/absence of melanosome hollowness and/or platelet shape.
source: For example, descriptions for only 61% of species included details about melanin layer thickness, while descriptions for almost all species had complete information on the presence/absence of melanosome hollowness and/or platelet shape (92%).
evidence: This is stated as a description of data completeness.

claim: Most species records (83%) described the type of structure (single-layered or photonic crystal).
source: Most species records (83%) described the type of structure (single-layered or photonic crystal).
evidence: This is stated as a description of data completeness.

claim: 280 species had enough data to be included in phylogenetic analyses.
source: Out of these, 280 species had enough data to be included in our phylogenetic analyses.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the data used in analyses.

claim: The phylogenies of Jetz et al., 2012 are based on a Hackett et al., 2008 backbone.
source: We used the phylogenies of Jetz et al., 2012, which are based on a Hackett et al., 2008 backbone, to construct a tree including all the species in the feather iridescence database and the species from the Li et al., 2012 data set.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the phylogenetic methods.

claim: Resolution was set to 80 pixels/µm in the optical modeling, which gives 12 sampling points for one 300 nm wave in the material with the highest refraction index (melanin).
source: Resolution was set to 80 pixels/µm, which gives 12 sampling points for one 300 nm wave in the material with the highest refraction index (melanin).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the optical modeling parameters.

claim: The extinction coefficient (k) of melanin was set to 0.1 in the optical modeling.
source: We set the extinction coefficient (k) of melanin to 0.1, the refractive index (n) of keratin to 1.56, and the refractive index of melanin to 2.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the optical modeling parameters.

claim: The refractive index (n) of keratin was set to 1.56 in the optical modeling.
source: We set the extinction coefficient (k) of melanin to 0.1, the refractive index (n) of keratin to 1.56, and the refractive index of melanin to 2.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the optical modeling parameters.

claim: The refractive index of melanin was set to 2 in the optical modeling.
source: We set the extinction coefficient (k) of melanin to 0.1, the refractive index (n) of keratin to 1.56, and the refractive index of melanin to 2.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the optical modeling parameters.

claim: 4500 unique structures were generated in the optical modeling (900 for each of the five melanosome types).
source: We generated 4500 unique structures (900 for each of the five melanosome types) that varied systematically in structural parameters (including diameter of melanosomes, lattice spacing, hollowness, and platelet shape; see full model description in Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the optical modeling approach.

claim: All simulated structures were modeled with four layers (the median number of layers for photonic crystals in the feather iridescence database).
source: For example, we modeled all simulated structures with four layers (the median number of layers for photonic crystals in the feather iridescence database), while real structures have varying numbers of layers, which would affect the brightness and saturation of colors independent of melanosome type.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the optical modeling approach.

claim: In the plumage data set, 38 species had a single layer and 42 species had a photonic crystal structure.
source: In our data set, 38 species had a single layer and 42 species had a photonic crystal structure.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the plumage data.

claim: Reflection from a multilayer with melanin and keratin becomes saturated at >9 layers.
source: Reflection from a multilayer with melanin and keratin becomes saturated at >9 layers (Land, 1972), so it is likely that the greatest advantage of hollowness is gained for structures with ≤9 layers.
evidence: This is stated as a fact with citation.

claim: The greatest advantage of hollowness is likely gained for structures with ≤9 layers.
source: Reflection from a multilayer with melanin and keratin becomes saturated at >9 layers (Land, 1972), so it is likely that the greatest advantage of hollowness is gained for structures with ≤9 layers.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on cited information.

claim: A near doubling of color diversity is observed for real plumage structures with thin melanin layers compared to structures with thick solid rods.
source: We observe a near doubling of color diversity for real plumage structures with thin melanin layers compared to structures with thick solid rods, consistent with the results of the optical model.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the plumage data analysis.

claim: Hollowness and a platelet shape increase the brightness of colors further, in agreement with the optical model.
source: Hollowness and a platelet shape increase the brightness of colors further, in agreement with the optical model.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the plumage data analysis.
